patches.old:
1. “Fear,” he says, “the Lord, and keep his commandments. By keeping the commandments of God you will be powerful in every deed, and your conduct will be beyond compare. For in fearing the Lord you will do everything well. This is the fear that you must have—and you will be saved.[a]

2. But do not fear the devil; for by fearing the Lord you will gain mastery over the devil, because there is no power in him. In the one who has no power, there is no fear; but in the one who has glorious power, there is also fear. For everyone who has power is feared, but the one who has no power is despised by all.[b]

3. But fear the works of the devil, for they are evil. So, by fearing the Lord, you will fear the works of the devil, and you will not do them, but will keep away from them.[c]

4. Therefore there are two fears: if you wish to do what is evil, fear the Lord and you will not do it; and if, on the other hand, you wish to do what is good, fear the Lord and you will do it. Thus the fear of the Lord is strong and great and glorious. So fear the Lord, and you will live for him; and all who fear him among those who keep his commandments will live for God.[d]

5. “Why,” I said, “sir, did you say about those who keep his commandments, ‘They will live for God’?” “Because,” he said, “all creation fears the Lord, but it does not keep his commandments. Therefore the life of those who fear him and keep his commandments is with God; but for those who do not keep his commandments, there is not even life in them.[e]”

patches.reason: Reconsideration of the prior lexical decision: independently against the supplied Greek, ἐν αὐτῷ is singular and the final clause does not explicitly say that the disobedient lack life within themselves. Restore the singular without deciding its referent.

patches.old: The final “in them” retains the existing English interpretation, also found in Vulgata printed51 (in illis). The working printed Greek and Lake1907 Plate VI line56 instead have singular en autō, “in him”; “there is not even life in him” is the more literal alternative, with God as one possible referent. Palatina printed97 paraphrases “will not be in life,” with an editor-supplied negation in its preceding do-not-fear clause. These differences are explicit rather than silently rewriting Greek to match Latin. All creation fearing and the further commandment-keeping condition are both retained; this bounded check does not independently certify the whole manuscript tradition.
patches.new: The final “in him” renders the singular Greek en autō. Its referent is not explicitly named; God is one possible referent. Reconsideration of the prior lexical decision: the earlier “in them” is no longer the main-text rendering. The supplied bounded comparison reports singular wording in Lake1907 Plate VI line56, plural in illis (“in them”) in Vulgata printed51, and “will not be in life” in Palatina printed97, with an editor-supplied negation in its preceding do-not-fear clause. The reported Latin plural remains an alternative, not the rendering of the selected Greek. All creation fearing and the further commandment-keeping condition are both retained; this bounded comparison does not independently certify the whole manuscript tradition.
